Each captured soul grants him a shield, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack of shield negates 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) damage. He converts 25% of his remaining shield to Health every second, gaining 1 Health for every 2 points of shield.

Upon landing, he swings his Crescent Halberd, dealing 650 (650 + 240% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. passive.description: Zhou Yu's Basic Attacks and skills place fire marks on enemies (including structures) for 4s. At 4 stacks, the marks ignite, dealing 125 (125 + 17% ) magical damage per second for 4s and reducing the target's Movement Speed by 15% for 1s. Targets cannot gain more marks while burning.

skill1.description: Zhou Yu invokes a wind domain. Teammates within the domain gain 5% Movement Speed (up to 5 heroes; effect doubled for Zhou Yu), while enemy heroes' Movement Speed are reduced by 10% for 3s. When the wind is invoked, enemies within range are knocked back in the target direction and take 200 (200 + 30% ) magical damage. If the wind domain overlaps with a fire domain for 1s, a new fire domain spreads in the target direction, dealing 100 (100 + 25% ) magical damage every 0.5s. This damage stacks with any existing fire domains.

skill2.description: Zhou Yu calls down a volley of flaming arrows at the target location, dealing 250 (250 + 40% ) magical damage and leaving behind a fire domain that lasts for 6.5s. The fire domain deals 100 (100 + 30% ) magical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s. There can be up to 6 fire domains present at any time, after which creating a new fire domain will extinguish the first one. Zhou Yu stocks 1 volley every 9s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), and up to 3 can be stocked. Passive: While inside a fire domain, he recovers 35 (35 + 7% + 2% extra ) Health every 0.5s.

skill3.description: Zhou Yu unleashes a burst of flames in the target area, dealing 200 (200 + 40% ) magical damage. If the flames travel through a fire domain, a firestorm is created, dealing an extra 200 (200 + 40% ) magical damage to enemies within range and stunning them for 1s.

strengths: His strength lies in combining Skill 2 with Skill 1 to create large burning zones that dish out powerful sustained magic damage. weaknesses: Spreading his burning zones requires comboing with Skill 1—on its own, the effect is limited. To trigger his powerful heat wave, he also needs to land Skill 3 inside a burning zone, which makes his setup predictable and easy for enemies to read and dodge.

passive.description: When Yango and the puppet's Basic Attacks hit an enemy hero, they have a 30% chance of granting a Hero Shard and restoring 70 (+1% extra Health) Health. Yango's Recovery skill is replaced with Hero Shards. He can stock up to 150 Hero Shards, which can be used to turn his puppet into a copy of an enemy hero. He automatically stocks 1 Hero Shard every 10–5s, depending on his level. Hero Puppet: Consumes 50 Hero Shards to transform the puppet into a copy of the selected hero for 10s. The hero puppet possesses all of the copied hero's skills, but only deals 50% damage and takes an extra 100% damage compared to them. The hero puppet becomes stronger with Yango, dealing 1% more damage for every 15 extra Physical Attack and taking 2% less damage for every 80 extra Health.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Occult Arts - Umbra / Occult Arts - Return

forms.description: Yango throws the puppet, dealing 300 (+100% extra physical damage) to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. He then starts controlling the puppet. The puppet's Basic Attacks deal 100% Physical Attack physical damage. When recalled, the puppet purifies crowd control effects from Yango and grants him 40% Movement Speed for 1s, as well as a shield that negates 420 (+6% extra Max Health) damage. When the puppet is destroyed, Yango is revealed and stunned for 2s. He is then unable to summon the puppet for 20–16s. If the puppet remains beyond a range of 2,500 from Yango for 5s, it is automatically destroyed. Normal Puppet: Inherits all of Yango's equipment effects (excluding Revive, Blood Fury, Dark Curtain, and Mana Shield), inherits certain buff effects, and shares Gold and EXP with him.
Retrieves the puppet immediately, dealing 300 (+100% extra physical damage) to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.5s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Occult Arts - Zhi Chu Luan / Occult Arts - Substitution

forms.skill_name: Skill 2: Occult Arts - Zhi Chu Luan
forms.description: Yango sends out 4 paper birds, dealing 435 (+165% extra physical damage) to enemies in their paths. When multiple paper birds hit the same target, the damage is reduced by 50% for subsequent hits.

The puppet swaps locations with Yango if it is within a range of 900 from him; otherwise, it will move to a location that is 900 from him, dealing 300 (+100% extra physical damage) to enemies in its path. If the puppet's movements have been restricted, this skill pulls Yango to the puppet and returns control to him.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Occult Arts - Shadow Crucifixion / Occult Arts - Binding

forms.description: Yango releases two strings then pulls them back, each string dealing 180 (+90% extra physical damage). Enemies hit by both strings take extra physical damage equal to 13% of lost Health and are slowed by 30% for 2s.

After a brief delay, the puppet will stun enemies continuously, with each strike dealing 120 (+40% extra physical damage) magical damage.

skill4.name: Skill 4: Occult Arts - Dispersal / Occult Arts - Breakout

forms.description: Yango instantly vanishes, cleansing all crowd control effects from himself, then reappears in the target location after a short delay. Does not cleanse the stun effect from the puppet being destroyed.

While enhanced, whenever he hits an enemy with a Basic Attack or skill, he recovers 220 (220 + 6% extra Health) Health. This passive effect can only be triggered once every 25s. skill1.description: Dun swings his blade, creating a gust of wind in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical damage) physical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25% for 2s. If the wind hits any enemy, he can use the skill again within 5s in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical damage) physical damage and launching enemies for 1s.

skill2.description: Dun deals 300 (300 + 100% extra magical damage) magical damage to nearby enemies and gains a shield that negates damage equal to 500 (500 + 12% extra Health) for 5s. His next 3 Basic Attacks are enhanced for 8s, dealing an extra 150 (150 + 45% extra true damage) true damage each. Hitting enemies reduces the cooldown of his Ultimate by 1s.

skill3.description: Dun throws his chained blade in the target direction, which stops upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range. The blade stuns the first enemy it hits for 1s. Dun deals 400 (400 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to enemies near the blade and pulls himself to its location. Upon reaching the blade's location, he deals 400 (400 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to nearby enemies again. Dun gains immunity to crowd control while using this skill.

skill2.description:
Lady Zhen fires a water orb at the target which bounces between nearby enemy units up to 5-7 times (max number increases when skill level reaches 3 and 5). Each bounce deals 230 (230 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies.

skill3.description:
Lady Zhen unleashes a water spirit in the target direction, knocking back non-hero units. Upon hitting an enemy hero or reaching its maximum range, the water spirit forms a pool, dealing 300 (300 + 65% magical attack) magical damage to the first hero hit and reducing their Movement Speed by 90% for 1s.
The pool lasts for 5s, dealing 150 (150 + 32% magical attack) magical damage every second to enemies in its range and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1.5s.

passive.description: Whenever Li Bai hits a non-structure enemy unit with his Basic Attack, he gains 1 Sword Energy, for up to 4 stacks. skill1.description:
Li Bai can dash twice in the target direction with Drunken Sword Style, dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.5s while gaining 1 Sword Energy. He returns to his original location after using the skill a third time.

skill2.description:
Li Bai conjures a Green Lotus Sword Formation around himself, dealing 200 (200 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
The sword formation deals 325 (325 + 115% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies touching its edge, while inflicting extreme slow for 1s and reducing their physical defense by 150 for 3s.
While creating the formation, Li Bai removes all debuffs from himself and becomes untargetable.
When he is inside the sword formation, he has a 10% chance to dodge Basic Attacks from enemies inside the formation (doubled for Basic Attacks dealt from outside the formation).

skill3.description:

148.name: Jiang Ziya

counters.reason: Can instantly close the gap with high mobility and stealth, easily one-shotting the immobile Jiang Ziya.

If Ziya acts as a support in the match, he grants additional Sanctification effects based on the teammate's class.

skill1.description: Ziya places a divine seal on enemies in the target area, dealing 70 (70 + 14% magical damage), followed by 60 (60 + 12% magical damage) every 0.4s for a total of 7 hits. Sealed enemies will gradually lose up to 30% of their Movement Speed and 10% of their Physical Defense and 10% of their Magical Defense. If the skill hits any enemy, he gains a 30% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s.

skill2.description: Ziya unleashes divine retribution on wrongdoers, conjuring a magic circle that deals 3 strikes of damage to enemies in the target area. Each strike deals 60 (60 + 12% magical damage). After a short delay, the magic circle explodes, dealing 300 (300 + 70% magical damage) to enemies and launching them for 0.75s.

skill3.description: Ziya channels divine energy in the target direction, unleashing 3 shockwaves. The first 2 shockwaves each deal 120 (120 + 20% magical damage), while the last deals 560 (560 + 80% magical damage). Each subsequent level gained increases the chance of entering the Sanctifier state by 20%. The charging lasts up to 2s, and moving or using the Ultimate again will immediately unleash the shockwaves. Charge time affects the attack range of the shockwaves, up to a distance of 1,800. Shockwaves deal 10% damage to structures in their path.

strengths: Han Xin's defining strength is his overwhelming mobility — among the very best in the game — with three movement skills (two charges of Skill 1 plus Skill 2). weaknesses: His base durability is extremely low, and once he gets caught by crowd control he can be killed before he does anything. He is also demanding to pilot — Skill 2's reverse-direction dash and other quirks give him a unique feel — so his performance depends enormously on the player's mechanics and map awareness.

Mulan draws her dual swords and makes a sweeping slash, dealing 377 (200 + 110% extra physical damage) to nearby enemies and gaining 60% Attack Speed for 5s. She gains 40 Movement Speed and can use her dual sword skills while her dual swords are drawn.

passive.description: Erin's Basic Attacks deal 20 (20 + 20% AD) physical damage and 20 (+20% AP) magical damage, granting her 1 stack of Energy. For every 100 AP she has over 2000, she gains an additional 0.5% Critical Rate.

skill1.description: Erin fires a ring of laurel leaves, dealing 300 (300 + 50% AD + 35% AP) magical damage. skill2.description: Erin instantly gains max Energy, immunity to slows, and 30% Attack Speed for 3s.

skill3.description: When Erin has max Energy, her ultimate is unlocked. Activating it consumes all Energy, increasing her Movement Speed by 10% and firing leaves at the enemy with the lowest Health (prioritizing heroes), dealing 40 (40 + 28% AD + 20% AP) magical damage. This skill can be used continuously while Erin moves. (Each leaf fired reduces Skill 2's cooldown by 0.2s).

passive.description: After Liang's Basic Attacks or skills deal damage to a target twice within 1.5s, he enters a state of continuous attack, during which he deals 120 (120 + 70% magical attack) true damage to the target every 1.2s.

skill1.description:
Liang summons 4 magical barriers at the target location. When touched by an enemy, barriers disappear and deal 360 (360 + 75% magical attack) magical damage while stunning the target for 0.75s. After the stun wears off, the enemy is slowed by 25% for 0.5s.
If the same enemy touches multiple barriers within a short period, subsequent barriers only deal half of the damage without the stun, and the enemy's is slowed by 25% for 1.25s.

skill2.description:
Liang conjures a circle of attrition at the target location for 5.5s. The circle deals 110 (110 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to 1 enemy within range every 0.5s and provides vision of the area. Non-hero enemy units take 50% more damage. He gains 60 Movement Speed while inside a circle of his.
He can have at most 2 circles up at the same time. He stocks 1 charge of the skill every 12s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 3 charges.

skill3.description:
Liang uses a Power Word to suppress an enemy hero for 2.2s and deal 100 (100 + 18% magical attack) magical damage to them every 0.5s.
If he finishes using this skill without being interrupted, a magic field is summoned at the target hero's location for 0.5s. Enemies that step into the field take 240 (240 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and are stunned for 0.75s.

strengths: Liang's greatest strength is his extremely powerful single-target suppression, lasting up to 2.2 seconds, which reliably neutralizes a chosen enemy. On top of that, Skill 2 offers strong wave clear and vision, Skill 1 provides AoE zoning and a stun, and his passive's ongoing true damage lets him hurt even heavily armored tanks. The movement speed boost he gains inside Skill 2's zone gives him solid mobility as well.
weaknesses: During his powerful Skill 3 suppression he cannot move either, leaving him defenseless and an easy focus target for other enemies mid-channel. Skill 1's stun cannot re-apply to the same enemy, so he cannot chain-stun multiple targets for long. His passive's true damage requires landing hits within 1.5-second intervals, which is hard to keep up against highly mobile enemies who constantly create distance.

skill1.description: Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction. At the end of the dash, she launches a flying kick, dealing 600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 0.75s. She recovers 25 Energy if an enemy is hit.

skill2.description: Mai Shiranui throws her fan in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy hit, slowing them immensely for 0.5s, and reducing their Magical Defense by 50 for 3s. She recovers 10 Energy if she hits an enemy. After landing a hit, the fan deals an equal amount of magical damage (halved against heroes) to the closest unit behind the target.

skill3.description: Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction, dealing 800 (800 + 110% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies in her path and knocking them back while reducing their Physical Attack by 20% for 2.5s. She recovers 25 Energy for each enemy hit.

strengths: Mai Shiranui packs a wealth of crowd control: a knock-up on Skill 1, a knockback on Skill 3, and another knockback on her empowered basic attack. Combined with Skill 2's magic defense shred and potent long-range poke, plus a roll after every skill or empowered attack, she boasts outstanding mobility and evasion. Skill 3 also debuffs the target's physical attack, making her single-target burst and disruption exceptional.
weaknesses: Her skills cost energy, and she cannot recover enough of it without landing hits, so a whiffed skill leaves her badly exposed. Failing to control her passive rolls can also carry her into dangerous positions. For all her CC and mobility, she has no defensive skills of her own — get caught by enemy crowd control and she melts in seconds.

synergy.reason: Dolia can reset his powerful AoE ultimate, allowing them to completely dominate teamfights.
Resetting her ultimate allows for extremely powerful chain-kill potential.

counters.reason: His strong lockdown abilities can disrupt her positioning, bursting her down before she has a chance to reset an ally's ultimate.
Can disrupt Dolia's supportive actions with continuous CC, severely reducing her impact in teamfights.

passive.description: Dolia takes the form of a mermaid while in water, reducing slow effects by 50% and recovering 60 (60 + 1% extra Health) Health and 5 Mana every second. Her Basic Attacks become splashes of water that deal area damage. Her Recovery skill becomes Mermaid's Gift, which can be used to form a covenant with a selected teammate. This teammate becomes the priority target for Celestial Melody.

skill1.description: Dolia sings, unleashing 4 soundwaves that spread out around her. The first 3 deal 130 (130 + 20% magical damage) magical damage and inflict a 7.5% slow. The 4th soundwave deals 250 (250 + 40% magical damage) magical damage and inflicts a 30% slow for 1s. This soundwave triggers echoes when hitting enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 24% magical damage) magical damage. While in water, it stirs up a wave that knocks back nearby enemies and stuns enemies next to her. Echoes triggered by non-hero units have a shorter range and only deal 50% damage.

skill2.description: Dolia leaps forward and transforms into a mermaid. If she lands on solid ground, she creates a pool of water and restores 320 (320 + 40% Health) Health to her and her nearby teammates. While in the pool, teammates recover Health and Mana at the same rate as Dolia's. Cooldown is reduced by 25% if used while in water. The pool disappears if she leaves it for 4s.

skill3.description: Dolia channels for a short time, resetting the cooldown of a skill for a teammate within range. The skill that gets reset is the one with the longest remaining cooldown. In return, Dolia takes on a Cooldown of 10 (+120% of the current skill Cooldown) seconds herself. If the teammate does not use the reset skill, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is reduced by 20%. If the teammate uses the reset skill within 5s, it does not consume Energy, and any earnings from defeating enemies with that skill are shared evenly with Dolia. This skill prioritizes the teammate with whom she has formed a covenant. If no teammates are nearby, she resets one of her own skills. If the reset fails, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is significantly reduced.

combos.description: Skill 2 -> Basic Attack -> Skill 1. Slap a heavy slow on pursuing enemies and buy your team the decisive seconds it needs to regroup.

strengths: Her one-of-a-kind Skill 3, which fully resets the cooldowns of an ally's powerful skills, is her defining strength. Skill 2's water zones grant sustained HP and mana regeneration not just to herself but to the whole team, giving her tremendous support power and staying power. Inside water, Skill 1 transforms into an AoE knockback and stun — a potent self-defense and disruption tool — making her uniquely dominant in fights around the river and other bodies of water.
weaknesses: Skill 3's cooldown depends heavily on the cooldown of her allies' skills, so it only shines right after a teammate has used a powerful ability — she is extremely reliant on what her team does. With no meaningful damage skills of her own, her solo combat power is very low.

passive.description: Nakoruru's next Basic Attack is enhanced after her skills hit an enemy, dealing extra physical damage.

Skill 1's marks deal max-HP percentage damage with high physical scaling for tremendous burst, and Skill 3's charge cuts the enemy's damage dealt by 30%, making her strong in extended trades. Skill 2's dash also heals her and deals bonus damage to monsters, giving her excellent jungle clear and sustain.
weaknesses: Caught by heavy crowd control, she falls quickly, as her durability is nothing special. Her kit is built entirely around diving in to deal damage, with little in the way of reliable escapes once committed, so she risks being stranded deep behind enemy lines. Her mana costs are steep — if she fails to collect Skill 1's marks to refund mana, she runs dry in no time.

Ukyo Tachibana's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a quick-draw slash that has longer range, dealing 40 (40 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15-30% (scales with hero level) for 2s. Ukyo Tachibana slashes in the target direction, dealing 580 (580 + 190% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.

The healing is halved if only non-hero units are hit.

Every skill he lands shortens his passive's cooldown, so his sustained mid-range damage output is superb as well.
weaknesses: His base durability is low, and Skill 3's healing only triggers on hit, so hard crowd control that stops him in his tracks gets him killed in an instant. Can easily secure assassinations from behind while Arthur keeps the enemies silenced.

Allies near marked enemies gain 10% Movement Speed.

skill2.description: Arthur summons holy shields that orbit him for 5s, dealing 285 (145 + 80% physical damage) every second to nearby enemies.

skill3.description: Arthur raises Excalibur and leaps at the target enemy hero, dealing magical damage equal to 16% of their max Health and leaving behind a holy seal. Enemies within range of the seal are launched for 0.5s. The seal lasts 5s and deals 85 magical damage to enemies within range every second.

Skill 1's movement speed boost into a targeted dash with silence is very easy to use and reliably shuts down enemy actions. Skill 3's magic damage equal to 16% of max HP also lets him hurt even armor-stacking tanks — a hero with simple controls yet impressive versatility.
weaknesses: As a melee hero who must get close to deal damage, he can be whittled down helplessly against long-range kiting specialists or team comps stacked with movement-restricting crowd control. He has no defensive skill to instantly negate enemy attacks, so diving too deep gets him focused down quickly, and he lacks a dedicated escape tool as well.

skill1.description:

He recovers 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) Health for each enemy hit by the slash. Effect is halved against non-hero units.

Skill 3's wide-area knockback and stun can flip a losing fight on its head, covering everything from engages to disengages. passive.name: Passive Skill: Forge Inheritor
passive.description:
Chicha cycles through her five ancestral weapons (polearm, spear, dagger-axe, halberd, and bow). Each Basic Attack restores 20 (20 + 0.3% extra Health) Health and switches to the next weapon with increased range. Each Basic Attack or skill hit grants 1 stack of Fighting Spirit (lasts 4s, up to 8 stacks), with each stack granting 4% Attack Speed (can exceed the Attack Speed cap).
Holding a polearm or spear puts her in Defense Form, dagger-axe or halberd puts her in Offense Form, and bow puts her in Overkill Form.
Each form grants different Skill 1 and Skill 2 effects. Entering Overkill Form instantly reduces Skill 1 and Skill 2 CD by 50%.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Peak-Crushing Polearm / Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe / Sky-Shattering Bow

forms.description: Defense Form: Chicha swings her weapon and leaps forward in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical damage) to enemies in the path and carrying them to the landing point. After landing, thrusts forward, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical damage) and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Offense Form: Chicha hurls her weapon toward the target direction and propels forward, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical damage) to enemies in her path and pushing them to the skill's endpoint. After landing, she smashes the ground, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical damage) and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Overkill Form: Chicha launches a flying kick in the target direction, firing a piercing arrow that deals 275 (275 + 90% extra physical damage) and knocking back enemies for 0.75s. If enemies hit a wall, they are restricted to a fixed area for 2s and take 275 (275 + 90% extra physical damage).

skill2.name: Skill 2: World-Splitting Spear / Realm-Sweeping Halberd / Star-Felling Arrow

forms.description: Defense Form: Chicha leaps forward and spins her weapon, pulling in nearby enemies and dealing 225 (225 + 80% extra physical damage). When hitting an enemy, she leaps backward, recovering 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health. While pulling in enemies, she gains crowd control immunity and 15% damage reduction.

Offense Form: Chicha sweeps in the target direction, dealing 475 (475 + 160% extra physical damage) and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

Overkill Form: Chicha aims in the target direction, locking onto all enemies in range (up to five, prioritizing heroes). After aiming, she shoots arrows at all locked-on targets, dealing 500 (500 + 170% extra physical damage), plus true damage equal to 10% of the Health the target has lost, and knocking back enemies (without crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
While using this skill, Chicha gains crowd control immunity and 15% damage reduction.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Return of the Armsmaster
skill3.description:
Chicha unleashes all five weapons, gaining a Movement Speed boost for 2s and 35% Attack Speed, and breaking the Fighting Spirit stack limit for 6s.
During this time, she commands all five weapons to attack, with each Basic Attack dealing an extra 40 (40 + 13% extra physical damage).
While using this skill, she can use her Basic Attack while moving. Overkill Form will remain active once entered.

strengths: Fang's greatest strength is arguably the fastest objective clearing of any hero — jungle camps, dragons, and towers alike — thanks to his passive's bonus monster damage and Skill 1's mark detonations. Rare for a marksman, Skill 2 lets him move while untargetable, a powerful self-defense tool, and combined with his passive's vision-granting effect it makes him remarkably hard to kill. Skill 3 adds wide-area zoning on top, rounding out a kit strong on both offense and defense.

And once Skill 2 is spent, his window of vulnerability is wide — get focused by multiple enemies then and he crumbles.

At the same time, he recovers 162 (96 + 40% magical damage + 2% Health) Health. When a dark orb hits a non-hero unit, he recovers 1% Health. He can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting him simultaneously.

skill1.description: Releases a burst of power, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical damage) magical damage to nearby enemies and creating a dark orb that orbits around him. Can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting simultaneously. When this skill hits an enemy, its Cooldown and Mana cost are reduced by 50%. If there are already 3 dark orbs present, restores 150 (150 + 60% magical damage) Health instead. The number of dark orbs will influence the strength of Dark Impact.

skill2.description: Donghuang consumes all of his dark orbs (there must be at least one) to barrage the target location, with each orb targeting a further area than the last. Orbs deal 500 (500 + 60% magical damage) magical damage to enemies within range. When he uses this skill, he gains 30% Movement Speed for 1s. He gains 10% Movement Speed for every extra dark orb consumed. The first orb slows enemies within range by 30% for 1s, the second slows enemies within range immensely for 1s, and the third will stun enemies within range for 1s.

skill3.description: Donghuang suppresses an enemy hero for 2s. While the enemy is suppressed by him, both share all damage taken. He instantly gains 3 dark orbs when his Ultimate is used. During suppression, the orbs orbit 25% faster. Every 50 Magical Attack makes them orbit 5% faster, to a max of 100%.

strategy.earlyGame: Playing Donghuang as a roamer, your early combat power is enormous. Invade the enemy jungle with Skill 1's orbs deployed — against clustered enemies your healing becomes absurd, letting you win 1v3 skirmishes outright. Secure the river crab in mid and make the enemy jungler's life miserable.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, your job is hard engages and objective control. Secure vision around the Tyrant and Overlord, and use Skill 2 for long-range harass, slows, and stuns. Always track the enemy carry's position and keep a Flash-into-Ultimate ready to go.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game you function as the ultimate anti-carry. Your mere presence forces the enemy to respect their positioning. Never waste your Ultimate on a tank — save it to reliably eliminate the enemy marksman or assassin. Stay glued to your damage dealers and play as their living shield.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, engage or counter-engage onto the most fed enemy threat. Flash into your Ultimate (Skill 3) is a guaranteed lockdown that pierces even crowd control immunity. While suppressing, the damage you take is shared with the target, so you will be relying on your team's burst damage to finish the job.

combos.title: Flash Suppression Combo
combos.description: Skill 1 (3 orbs) -> Skill 2 -> Flash -> Skill 3. Launch your orbs to stun the enemy, instantly Flash to close the distance, and lock them down with a guaranteed Ultimate.

combos.title: Invade & Sustain
combos.description: Skill 1 (keep 3 orbs up) -> Basic Attack -> Skill 1. Stick close to multiple enemies to maximize the healing from your dark orbs while weaving in basic attacks.

strategy.commonMistakes: Using your Ultimate on a high-HP tank instead of a squishy priority target. Or diving in alone into positions where your teammates cannot follow.

strengths: His greatest strength is Skill 3's suppression — a guaranteed single-target death sentence that not even Purify can remove. No matter how fed the target is, once you catch them, the damage share lets you drag them down with you by force, so the possibility of a comeback is always alive. His passive dark orbs deal percentage damage and heal him, making him astonishingly tough in early close-range brawls, and giving him the overwhelming invade power to wreck the enemy jungle single-handedly.
weaknesses: Against long-range poke comps or highly mobile enemies who never step into orb range, he is completely helpless. He must land orbs at close range to heal, so getting chipped down from distance sinks him with ease. During Skill 3's suppression he cannot move either, so using it while surrounded by enemies is an invitation to get killed one-sidedly. Skill 2 also lands after a delay of a few seconds and must be aimed predictively or it gets dodged — a symptom of his overall lack of mobility.

synergy.reason: Perfectly follows up your group pull with devastating AoE burst damage.
Massive AoE burst damage perfectly synergizes with your pull and lockdown combo.

counters.reason: Uses i-frames to dodge your pull and counters with heavy burst damage.
Strong long-range CC stops your engage attempts dead in their tracks before you can get close.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: The Laws of Nature
passive.description: After Guiguzi leaves the enemy's field of vision for 3s, his next Basic Attack will be enhanced, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical damage) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25%-50% (increases with level) for 1.5s. If he is not in the enemy's field of vision when using the enhanced Basic Attack, this skill's CD will be increased to 10s.

skill1.description: Guiguzi covers himself in spriteflies that camouflage him from enemy sight for 4s. While camouflaged, he gains 40% Movement Speed and deals 450 (450 + 60% magical damage) magical damage to each enemy he touches, while reducing their Physical Defense and Magical Defense by 25% for 4s. This effect can only be triggered once on each enemy. The camouflage disappears when he deals damage to enemies in any other way.

skill2.description: Guiguzi summons a large number of spriteflies that surround him, dealing 100 (100 + 15% magical damage) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s to enemies within range, after which he pulls them in and stuns them for 1s, dealing 400 (400 + 60% magical damage) magical damage. If an enemy hero is hit, Guiguzi and teammates within range gain a shield that negates 600 (600 + 120% magical damage) damage.

skill3.description: Guiguzi orders spriteflies to cover himself and teammates within a range of 1,500, camouflaging everyone after 1s. The camouflage lasts for 4s, during which he and his teammates gain 30% Movement Speed and vision of the nearest enemy hero. While camouflaged, using Basic Attacks, skills, or inflicting debuffs on enemies will immediately remove it.

strategy.earlyGame: Guiguzi is a playmaking support who thrives on aggressive rotations. Help shove the mid wave quickly, then immediately look to gank the side lanes. With camouflage and bonus movement speed, you can run terrifying roams from the opening minutes — keep manufacturing numbers advantages.
strategy.midGame: Dominate the map through the mid game with relentless ambushes. Your Ultimate (Skill 3) grants camouflage to your entire team and reveals the nearest enemy — a powerful pick tool. Coordinate with your jungler to set up picks before objectives and dictate the tempo of the match.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, your main duties are vision control and flawless initiation. A well-timed five-man camouflage will thoroughly shatter the enemy formation. Just be careful never to engage too far from your team — you are fragile, and allied follow-up is non-negotiable.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, cloak your team with your Ultimate, then pass through enemies with Skill 1 to shred their physical and magic defense. Next, charge Skill 2 to drag every nearby enemy into one spot. The moment they clump together, have your team drop massive AoE damage on top of them.

combos.title: Invisible Vacuum
combos.description: Skill 3 -> Skill 1 -> Skill 2 -> Flash (optional). Cloak your team, pass through enemies to shred their defenses, and time Skill 2's detonation to pull them together. If needed, Flash at the last moment to adjust your position.

combos.title: Ambush Setup
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Skill 2 -> Basic Attack. Close in under camouflage and start the pull timer. Land your empowered basic attack for the slow to guarantee the pull connects.

strategy.commonMistakes: Mistiming the start of Skill 2's charge and whiffing the pull. Engaging solo when no teammates are in range to attack.

strengths: His greatest strengths are Skill 3's team-wide camouflage and Skill 2's pull-and-stun — an initiation package with overwhelming power. He can force-start teamfights before the enemy has any chance to react, carrying the potential to flip a game in a single moment. Skill 1's percentage shred of both physical and magic defense is also excellent, amplifying his entire team's damage. With the mobility to pressure the whole map non-stop, he is the pinnacle of aggressive supports.
weaknesses: His defensive stats are low and he leans on Skill 2's shield, so a failed engage usually means being instantly deleted with no escape — a genuinely high-risk design. Team coordination is an absolute requirement; in solo queue or on uncommunicative teams, his strengths go completely to waste. If his damage and CC miss, he has nothing left to offer and fades into irrelevance. Enemies with wide-area CC or vision-reveal skills also neutralize his tricks with ease.

synergy.reason: Hard CC guarantees lockdown on enemies, allowing Kongming to safely land his combo and ultimate.

counters.reason: Can invade early when mobility is low to apply pressure and disrupt Kongming's farm.
Can survive the burst damage and stick tightly to shut down Kongming's mobility.

passive.description: Kongming gains 1 mark for 10s every time his active skills hit an enemy, for up to 5 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, he summons 5 prisms, which circle around him for 10s and attack the nearest enemy unit, dealing 135 (135 + 25% magical attack) magical damage. Prisms prioritize enemy heroes. They deal 40% less damage to monsters and 40% extra damage to minions.

skill1.description: Kongming fires 3 prisms in the target direction, each dealing 450 (450 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. When multiple prisms hit the same enemy, subsequent hits only deal 20% damage. Each prism triggers 1 Strategic Mark. He stocks Arcane Assault every 7.5s, for up to 2 charges.

skill2.description: Kongming blinks in the target direction, creating magic fields at the start and the end of the dash that each deal 350 (350 + 52% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. When an enemy takes damage twice from this skill within 5s, they are inflicted with extreme slow. This effect diminishes over 3s. When an enemy takes damage from multiple fields at the same time, the second magic field only deals 50% damage. He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 7.5s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.

skill3.description: Kongming targets an enemy and starts channeling a Spirit Bomb, which deals 450 (450 + 55% magical attack) magical damage. Non-hero enemy units that are targeted or in the Spirit Bomb's path will take extra damage and be launched for 0.5s. Enemies take 2% extra damage from Spirit Bombs for every 1% Health lost. When a Spirit Bomb hits and defeats an enemy hero, Kongming gains a full stack of marks, and this skill's CD is reduced by 80%. If the targeted enemy hero is defeated while the Spirit Bomb is being channeled, the CD of this skill will still be reduced by 80%.

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Kongming operates as a high-mobility assassin mage in the mid lane or jungle. He depends heavily on snowballing off his Ultimate, so farm efficiently toward level 4. Stack your passive on minions and neutral monsters before joining fights, and you can unleash ferocious poke damage.
strategy.midGame: The mid game is your stage. Kills with your Ultimate massively refund its cooldown, so hunt low-HP targets relentlessly. Orbit the edges of teamfights, repositioning with Skill 2 while poking with Skill 1, and the moment someone drops into execute range, dive in and chase the reset.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, enemies stack magic defense and fights grow denser — extreme patience is required. Never dive in first. Wait for the enemy's key skills to fall, then strike: a single Ultimate reset can chain into a full team wipe.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, poke with Skill 1 and keep your passive stacked. Save Skill 2's blink for defense or for opening a line of fire. Fire your Ultimate at the squishiest or most wounded enemy — and if an enemy tank tries to body-block it, shift your angle with Flash or Skill 2.

combos.title: Execute Reset
combos.description: Skill 2 -> Skill 1 -> Skill 3. Blink to the ideal range, land Skill 1 point-blank to instantly fill your passive, then immediately fire your Ultimate at the low-HP target to secure the kill and the reset.

combos.title: Passive Poke
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Skill 2 (retreat) -> passive detonation. Catch minions and enemies with Skill 1 to build stacks, blink back to safety, and let your auto-tracking passive orbs deliver the damage for you.

strategy.commonMistakes: Using your Ultimate on a target you cannot finish off and losing the reset. Force-blinking into the frontline with Skill 2 and dying instantly to hard CC.

strengths: His strengths are the high mobility of Skill 2 and the steady damage output of his passive's auto-tracking orbs. Skill 3's damage scales with the target's missing HP, and kills grant a huge cooldown refund plus instant passive activation, giving him explosive potential to chain kill after kill.
weaknesses: Skill 3 can be blocked by other enemy heroes or non-hero units, so there is always a risk the intended target survives. And for all his blinks, his base durability is low — caught by enemies with no Skill 2 stacks in reserve, his odds of escaping alive are extremely slim.

synergy.reason: Combines strong basic attacks and CC to fully capitalize on Da Qiao's rapid engages and disengages.
Teleporting allies in to follow up on Mulan's ambushes gives a huge advantage in teamfights.

counters.reason: Exceptional mobility allows him to dive the backline and burst Da Qiao down before she can support her team.
High disengage capabilities make it easy to negate Da Qiao's ultimate summons.

passive.description:
Da Qiao boosts her own Movement Speed by 30.
When the koi in Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge leaps past another skill's tide, it triggers a tide explosion, dealing 140 (140 + 25% [icon]) magical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1s.
For every 250 Magical Attack, the skill range of Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge increases by 50, with a maximum increase of 200.

skill1.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 55% [icon]) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 75 (75 + 12% [icon]) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s. Using skills increases Da Qiao's Movement Speed by 30% for 2.5s.

skill2.description:
Da Qiao conjures a magic circle for 4s that grants vision. When it closes, she teleports a teammate to the spawn point, removing all debuffs. They can return via the portal at the Crystal.
If no hero teleports, the magic circle leaves behind a mark a teammate can touch to recall.
Using the skill again clears the mark. If no hero has teleported, 50% [icon] is returned. Da Qiao teleports first. No channeling is required to touch the recall mark.

skill3.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps from left to right, dealing 300 (300 + 55% [icon]) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 75 (75 + 12% [icon]) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s.

skill4.description: Da Qiao summons a whirlpool at the target location, dealing 500 (500 + 90% [icon]) magical damage to enemies within range. The whirlpool lasts for 8s, during which teammates can teleport to it by tapping the Eye of the Whirlpool button. Da Qiao and teammates gain a shield that negates 350 (350 + 50% [icon]) damage while in the whirlpool. Da Qiao gains an extra shield that negates damage equal to 7% of her extra [icon].

strategy.earlyGame: Da Qiao is a support who commands the game at the macro level. Early on, use Skill 3 and Skill 1 to help your mid laner clear waves and harass the enemy. Skill 2 lets you instantly recall a low-HP ally for a full heal, turning wars of attrition overwhelmingly in your favor.
strategy.midGame: Global mobility rules the mid game. Coordinate with your Clash Laner's split push, and the moment the enemy moves to answer it, use your Ultimate to summon your entire team to the objective on the opposite side of the map. Map-wide awareness and decision-making are your greatest weapons.
strategy.lateGame: Small mistakes in the late game lead straight to defeat — but Da Qiao never lets her team take a bad fight. When sieging, pre-place Skill 2 so wounded allies can return to base and immediately rejoin through your Ultimate. This builds an inexhaustible siege line that simply never falls.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, hold the backline and lay down Skill 3 to silence enemy skill casts. Use Skill 1 to knock away anyone diving onto your marksman. Place Skill 2 not directly under your carry but one step away — close enough to step into in an emergency. Deploy your Ultimate safely in the rear to call in reinforcements.

combos.title: Elevator Tactic (Recall & Return)
combos.description: Skill 2 -> Skill 3 (Ultimate). Place a recall circle for a low-HP ally and immediately deploy your Ultimate nearby. Your ally heals to full at base and rides the portal straight back into the fight.

combos.title: Disruptive Peel
combos.description: Skill 3 -> Skill 1. Lay the silence zone where the enemy assassin will land to shut down their burst, then immediately knock them back with the tide to protect your team.

strategy.commonMistakes: Placing Skill 2 under a healthy ally and accidentally recalling them in the middle of a winning teamfight. Dropping your Ultimate in the center of enemy AoE and summoning your team into a death trap.

strengths: Skill 2's instant ally recall-and-return is her defining strength — she excels at snatching teammates back from certain death. She also packs two kinds of knock-ups across Skills 1 and 3 along with AoE slows from her tide bursts, and her skill areas expand as her magic attack grows — a remarkably powerful scaling quirk.
weaknesses: Her personal damage output is low, and her entire kit assumes coordination with teammates. Skill 2's circle in particular takes 4 seconds from activation to teleport, so it cannot always save allies from sudden burst damage. And if teammates do not understand how her circles work, her true value never materializes.

synergy.reason: Strong shields and peel can fully protect a stationary Huang Zhong from enemy dives during his ultimate.
Holds the frontline and provides chain CC, creating a safe zone for Huang Zhong to fire his artillery.

counters.reason: High mobility allows him to poke from outside Huang Zhong's range and then dive in for burst damage.
Can deal massive damage with high-powered snipes from outside Huang Zhong's ultimate range, winning trades completely.

passive.description: Huang Zhong's Basic Attacks increase his physical attack by 6-12 and Critical Rate by 0.75%-1.5% (increases with hero level) for 1.5s, for up to 5 stacks. These buffs are doubled when he is in Turret Mode. When he enters or exits Turret Mode, the buffs' durations are refreshed, and the buff multiplier is replaced with the multiplier of the current mode.

skill1.description: Huang Zhong unleashes his potential, gaining 70% Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s. If he is in Turret Mode, he can leave it immediately. Passive: He gains 20 physical attack (doubled while the skill is active).

skill2.description: Huang Zhong places a landmine at the target location that grants him vision around it. The landmine deals 360 (360 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies that come into contact with it, while also granting him vision of them for 3s. The landmine slows heroes by 25% and inflicts 10%-20% Sunder for 2s (value scales with skill level). At the same time, he gains a shield that negates 360 (360 + 5.5% extra max health) damage for 3s. While not in Turret Mode, he gains increased skill use speed if there are enemies within range. Up to 2 landmines can exist at the same time.

skill3.description: Huang Zhong dashes for a certain distance and deploys a turret. For the next 15s, he is immobile and gains 200 physical defense and 200 magical defense. Each of his Basic Attacks deals 350 physical damage to enemies at the center (40% less to enemies on the edge). He returns to his normal mode after 5-9 Basic Attacks (number scales with skill level). Damage to towers is reduced by 50%. Passive: When he enters Turret Mode, the cooldown of Unleash Your Potential will be refreshed. Using the skill again allows him to exit Turret Mode.

strategy.earlyGame: Huang Zhong is a hyper-late-game Farm Lane marksman. Play defensively early and commit fully to farming. Place Skill 2 mines in the river bushes for vision, and use their shield to survive ganks. Only take trades when your passive stacks are fully built.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, as your crit and attack speed core items come together, your damage climbs visibly. Rotate with your team and use your Ultimate to siege towers safely — it can attack from outside tower range, making it the finest siege engine in the game. Never deploy without vision from your support.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Huang Zhong is an unstoppable monster. The seven volleys of your Ultimate can annihilate an entire enemy team. But you are completely rooted while deployed, so positioning is everything. Only set up your Ultimate once your team has built a solid defensive line around you.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, hold the absolute back row. Place Skill 2 traps at chokepoints or at your own feet to prep the shield and slow. Adjust your position with Skill 1's movement speed boost, and only deploy your Ultimate after the enemy's hard engage skills are spent, or from a safe spot behind a wall.

combos.title: Fortified Siege
combos.description: Skill 2 -> Skill 3 -> Basic Attack. Place a mine at the edge of your range to slow incoming threats, then deploy your Ultimate and rain shellfire down from beyond tower range.

combos.title: Kite & Reposition
combos.description: Basic Attack -> Skill 2 -> Skill 1 -> Basic Attack. Toss a mine at your pursuer for the shield and slow, dash away with Skill 1 to open distance, then turn and resume firing once you are safe.

strategy.commonMistakes: Deploying your Ultimate too early in a teamfight with enemy assassins unaccounted for, turning yourself into a free target. Forgetting to use Skill 1 to instantly cancel your Ultimate and escape.

strengths: Skill 3's turret mode delivers overwhelming wide-area damage, and his passive's self-buffs (bonus physical attack and crit rate) form his greatest strengths. Skill 2 adds vision control and a shield, while Skill 1 grants a strong movement speed boost — a powerful marksman who comes with genuine self-defense tools.
weaknesses: He cannot move at all in turret mode, making him extremely vulnerable to mobile assassins and mages who can attack from beyond his range. His damage to towers is reduced by 50%, so plan your sieges accordingly. And to unleash his full power, he depends enormously on team protection and careful positioning.

synergy.reason: Provides attack and movement speed buffs that greatly enhance Kaizer's single-target burst and chase potential.
Provides shields and CC to boost Kaizer's survivability and mobility, enabling him to run rampant in teamfights.

counters.reason: Denies Kaizer's engage while dealing continuous damage, allowing her to easily kite him in a 1v1.
Hard suppression ultimate completely locks Kaizer down before he can wreak havoc with his ultimate.

passive.description: Kaizer's Basic Attacks and Skill 2 deal 50% more physical damage when hitting only a single enemy.

skill1.description: Kaizer throws a blade in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and slowing them immensely for 1s. The blade then ricochets between nearby enemies (hitting each enemy only once), with each hit dealing an equal amount of damage and slowing the target by 15% for 2s. If the blade hits at least one enemy or finishes ricocheting, it returns to him, and he recovers 350 (350 + 5% extra Health) Health. This skill's CD is also reduced by 30%, and he gains 15% Attack Speed and 15% Movement Speed for 3s.

skill2.description: Kaizer slashes twice in the target direction, with each slash dealing 160 (160 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The second slash launches enemies for 1s. His next Basic Attack is enhanced, causing him to dash toward the target and deal 130 (130 + 35% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. Passive: After leaving combat, he gains 10 Movement Speed and recovers 1% Health and max Mana every second.

skill3.description: Kaizer summons his demonic suit of armor. After a 1s delay, he deals 250 (250 + 25% extra magical damage) magical damage to nearby enemies and enhances himself for 8s. While enhanced, he gains 500 Health, 100 physical attack, 50 Movement Speed, and 60 Block, while also dealing 50 (50 + 16% extra magical damage) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Kaizer is a Clash Lane and jungle fighter with exceptional 1v1 potential. Use Skill 1 to poke and heal, sustaining your way through lane. His passive boosts basic attack and Skill 2 damage by 50% against isolated targets, so always look to drag enemy heroes away from their minion wave before you fight.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, with your core items and Ultimate online, you become a terrifying duelist. Flank the enemy backline or catch enemies mid-rotation in the jungle. During your Ultimate, your attack, movement speed, and damage block all surge dramatically — you can out-stat almost anyone on the map through sheer brute force.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, durable as you are, don't mindlessly charge into all five enemies. Play like a frontline assassin: swing around the flank, wait for the initiation, then activate your Ultimate and make a beeline for the enemy marksman or mage. Late-game Kaizer crushes squishy targets in two hits.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, wait in a flanking bush. Throw Skill 1 to slow the target and speed yourself up. Activate your Ultimate (Skill 3) for the stat surge, close the distance with Skill 2's knock-up, and erase your target in an instant with empowered basic attacks.

combos.title: Demon God's Execution
combos.description: Skill 3 -> Skill 1 -> Skill 2 -> Empowered Basic Attack. Transform with your Ultimate, throw your blade for the slow, dive in with Skill 2's knock-up, and land a devastating empowered slash.

combos.title: Flash Engage
combos.description: Skill 2 -> Flash -> Empowered Basic Attack -> Skill 1. Flash during Skill 2's cast animation to land a surprise knock-up on an out-of-range target, land your slash, then chase with Skill 1.

strategy.commonMistakes: Engaging while your Ultimate is still on cooldown. Fighting inside a huge minion wave and wasting your 50% isolated-target damage bonus from your passive.

strengths: Devastating single-target burst and Skill 3's dramatic stat surge are his defining strengths. Skill 1's percentage healing and Skill 2's out-of-combat regeneration give him superb lane sustain, and with damage block and movement speed boosts on top, he is a fighter of unmatched strength in one-on-one duels.
weaknesses: His damage output is skewed heavily toward single targets, so when enemies cluster together he struggles to leverage his passive's bonus damage. And once his powerful Skill 3 expires, his combat strength drops off a cliff — mistime your engage and you will not survive the enemy's counterattack.

synergy.reason: Guaranteed hard CC locks targets down, ensuring Xuance's hook combos land perfectly.
Provides CC cleanse and damage reduction to prevent Xuance from being locked down and bursted when diving.

counters.reason: Instantly provides shields and damage reduction to targeted backliners with his ultimate, completely denying Xuance's kill.
Strong silence and instant burst damage can delete Xuance before he can even chain his skill combo.

passive.description: Basic attacks deal extra damage and grant movement speed.

skill1.description: Dashes forward, enhancing attack power.

skill2.description: Throws hook to bind an enemy. Can be reactivated to toss the enemy behind.

skill3.description: Dashes through the hooked target, dealing massive physical damage.

strategy.earlyGame: Xuance is a high-tempo jungle assassin who lives and dies by the snowball. Start at the red buff and hunt aggressive ganks at level 2 or level 4. Your entire kit hinges on landing Skill 2's hook — if you miss it, retreat immediately. Securing early kills to trigger your passive's frenzy state is critical.
strategy.midGame: Dominate the map by picking off isolated targets. Charge Skill 2 from out of vision, use the movement speed boost to close in, and hook the enemy carry. Recast Skill 2 to fling them behind you, then pass through them with your Ultimate for damage. Your mid-game burst is lethal to squishy targets.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, teamfights are extremely dangerous if you cannot secure a fast kill. Play as an opportunistic executioner: wait for the enemy to burn their CC, then hook a low-HP target and steal the kill. A kill or assist triggers your passive, granting massive attack speed and movement speed to sweep up the rest.
strategy.teamfight: Never engage first. Circle the outer edge of the fight charging Skill 2, waiting for a clear line to the marksman or mage. Once you hook them, drag them out of their safety net. The absolute key to your teamfight is securing that first kill or assist to trigger Frenzy — once it's live, you can play like a hyper carry.

combos.title: Shoulder-Throw Execute
combos.description: Skill 2 (charged hit) -> Skill 1 -> Skill 2 (throw) -> Skill 3 -> Basic Attack. Hook the target, reel them in slightly with Skill 1, recast Skill 2 to fling them behind you, then pass through them with your Ultimate while hammering in basic attacks.

combos.title: Chase & Reposition
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Skill 2 (charge) -> Skill 3 (while hooked). Close the gap with Skill 1 and immediately start charging Skill 2. With a target hooked, orbit around them with your Ultimate to dodge enemy skillshots.

strategy.commonMistakes: Continuing the fight after missing Skill 2's hook. Diving first into a CC-heavy comp and getting stunned to death before your passive ever activates.

strengths: His strengths are Skill 2's lockdown and forced displacement (the throw), Skill 3's dash with its high mobility and damage reduction, and the overwhelming attack speed and movement speed buff he gains from kills and assists. Once he creates an opening, he has the explosive power to collapse the entire enemy team in a single chain.
weaknesses: Everything depends on the accuracy of Skill 2 — miss the hook and he weakens drastically, making him a hero that demands very high mechanical skill. He is also vulnerable to hard CC like stuns: with his mobility locked down, his fragile durability is exposed, and he constantly risks getting deleted before his passive ever comes online.

synergy.reason: Long-range stuns lock enemies down, making it extremely easy for Shouyue to land his snipes.
Holds the frontline with heavy CC, buying plenty of time for Shouyue to safely snipe.

counters.reason: Her physical immunity skill allows her to completely negate Shouyue's snipe damage.
Provides shields and damage reduction to snipe targets via his ultimate, blocking potential kills.

passive.description:
Shouyue gains 1 stack of Ambush for every 1.5s he is out of combat, for up to 5 stacks. When he has Ambush stacks, he gains 20% Physical Pierce and 70-140 (+ 15% extra physical attack) physical damage. Every Basic Attack hit on enemy heroes consumes 1 stack of Ambush, while every skill hit consumes 5 stacks.
Accuracy: For every 1% Critical Rate, he deals 4 extra damage with Wild Wind and 2 extra damage with Getaway.

skill1.description:
Places a scouting device that provides vision within a range of 600-1,000 for 300s. He stocks 1 device every 35s, for up to 3 devices. Devices become ineffective when occupied by enemy heroes, and they become ineffective more quickly when occupied by multiple enemy heroes.
Passive: When out of combat and near natural terrain or a scouting device, he disguises himself, gaining 15% Movement Speed and 15% Attack Speed. After losing his disguise, the Attack Speed boost will remain in effect for 3s.

skill2.description:
Takes aim and snipes in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to targets hit, plus extra physical damage equal to 8% of the target's max health while slowing them immensely for 0.5s.
Aiming takes 2s, and bullets fired before the full duration have reduced accuracy. Up to 3 bullets can be stocked at a time. Landing a Basic Attack hit reduces the time taken to aim by 4%.
Wild Wind: When his Attack Speed is increased by 40%/80%/120%/160%, his aim time is reduced by 0.25/0.5/0.75/1s. The time taken for him to exit the aiming state is also reduced.

skill3.description:
Leaps backward and fires in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies in the path by 15% for 2s. Upon landing, gains 15% Movement Speed for 2s. Bullets stocked are shared with Wild Wind, and 1 bullet is used with each skill use.
Using Basic Attacks or skills removes the Movement Speed boost instantly.
Passive: Increases Basic Attack range by 15 with every skill level upgrade.

strategy.earlyGame: Shouyue is a lethal sniper for the Farm Lane or mid. Use your passive camouflage along walls to approach the lane safely. Early Skill 2 hits absurdly hard — hide your laser sight by aiming backward or into a wall, then flick it onto the enemy for massive damage. Suppress the lane with relentless poke.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, vision is your top priority. Placing Skill 1's vision devices at jungle crossroads and in river bushes will shut ganks down completely. Keep poking enemies under their tower with Skill 2 to force recalls, letting your team take objectives without resistance.
strategy.lateGame: Your job is to cut the enemy carry in half before the teamfight even begins. A single accurate late-game snipe removes half the HP bar of an enemy mage or marksman. Your passive converts crit rate into raw physical attack, so actively weave in your hard-hitting basic attacks between snipes.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, snipe from far in the back. Never let enemies close the gap. If an assassin dives you, immediately use your Ultimate to deal burst damage while leaping backward with a slow attached. When enemies are too close to safely charge a snipe, fall back on your extremely powerful basic attacks.

combos.title: Flick Snipe
combos.description: Aim Skill 2 in the opposite direction -> flick the cursor onto your target -> fire. Hiding the warning laser line until the instant you shoot makes the snipe nearly impossible to dodge.

combos.title: Anti-Assassin Counter
combos.description: Basic Attack -> Skill 3 (Ultimate) -> Skill 2. Land a basic attack on the diving assassin, immediately leap backward with your Ultimate while slowing them, then finish the job with a quick-cast Skill 2.

strategy.commonMistakes: Fixating on Skill 2 snipes even in close combat and ignoring your super-high-damage basic attacks. Holding your laser sight in plain view of the enemy so your shots get dodged with ease.

strengths: His greatest strengths are Skill 1's wide-area vision control with up to three devices, and Skill 2's massive snipe damage delivered from beyond retaliation range. Terrain-based concealment and Skill 3's backward leap with invulnerability give him remarkable self-preservation, making him a marksman with truly dominant presence.
weaknesses: His attack speed and crit rate convert through unusual formulas, so he lacks the sustained basic-attack DPS of a conventional marksman. Missing his Skill 2 snipes causes his damage contribution to plummet, and against mobile assassins who close the distance he has nothing but Skill 3 to answer with — once caught, he is extremely fragile.

synergy.reason: Strong CC locks enemies down, helping to keep them trapped inside Yixing's ultimate.
Can easily dive in and clean up kills on enemies trapped by Yixing's massive ultimate.

counters.reason: Extreme mobility allows him to dodge Yixing's skills and dive the backline for an instant kill.
Uses i-frames and high mobility to easily navigate Yixing's zone, avoiding CC while dealing damage.

passive.description:
Yixing's Basic Attacks deal magical damage, and skill hits apply 1 stack of Anti-Qi. At 4 stacks, a Weiqi stone is summoned below the enemy, dealing 100 (100 + 10% AP) magical damage. This Weiqi stone is then pulled to the center of Skill 2's Weiqi formation, dealing 170 (170 + 11% AP) magical damage to enemies in its path. He gains 1 permanent Weiqi stone every time Anti-Qi marks are triggered, as well as 5 Weiqi stones every 60s and whenever he scores a kill or assist. Each permanent Weiqi stone grants 1 AP.
When taking fatal damage, he enters the void, summoning a Weiqi stone below his feet while gaining immunity to all damage and 30% Movement Speed for 1s. This effect has a cooldown of 150s.
When Weiqi stones summoned by Anti-Qi marks hit an enemy multiple times within a short duration, subsequent hits deal only 50% damage.

skill1.description:
Places a Weiqi stone at the target location, gaining vision around it for 3s, dealing 100 (100 + 18% AP) magical damage, and reducing Taking Liberties' cooldown by 0.5s. The Weiqi stone lasts for 12s, and if a Weiqi formation is created, it will be pulled toward its center, dealing 180 (180 + 36% AP) magical damage to enemies in its path while slowing them by 25% for 1s. Hitting an enemy in this way will enhance his Basic Attack to deal 223 (120 + 60% AD + 18% AP) magical damage.
At 50/110/181 permanent Weiqi Stones, he gains an extra one-off skill that further improves his enhanced Basic Attack and grants a burst of Movement Speed for 5s. The enhanced Basic Attack improvements are a scattershot effect/17% damage boost/34% damage boost.
He stocks 1 Weiqi stone every 6s, for up to 2 stones. If an enemy is hit by multiple Weiqi stones being pulled to the Weiqi formation within 0.5s, subsequent hits only deal 50% of the initial damage. On-hit effects of enhanced Basic Attacks are reduced to 30%.

skill2.description:
Yixing deals 160 (160 + 25% AP) magical damage in the target area, which expands into a Weiqi formation. Enemies within the central area take 160 (160 + 25% AP) extra magical damage and are pulled toward the center of the formation.
The Weiqi formation lasts 10s. If Yixing passes through the formation's edge, he gains a 50% Movement Speed increase that diminishes over 1s, while enemy heroes that do so gain a stack of Anti-Qi. Each effect can only be triggered once. If Yixing moves too far away from the formation, it disappears.
This skill deals 180% more damage to non-hero units.

skill3.skill_name: Skill 3: The World is My Board
skill3.description:
Yixing's position becomes the corner of a void Weiqi board. After 1.5s, the board takes shape and launches enemies within it for 0.5s. The Weiqi board lasts for 4s, during which enemy heroes cannot leave it. The board adds 3 Anti-Qi marks to enemy heroes over time and exposes their location. If he successfully traps an enemy hero, he gains 1 charge of Sliding Stones.
The smaller the Weiqi board, the shorter the cooldown, for a maximum reduction of 25%.
When the Weiqi board is fully formed, Yixing gains 30-70% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Yixing is a mid lane control mage who commands the battlefield with Go stones. Focus on fast wave clear by colliding your black and white stones (Skill 1 and Skill 2). Use the movement speed boost from stone collisions to rotate safely to the side lanes and support your teammates.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, your area control in narrow jungle corridors and around objectives is frightening. Poke constantly with your stones — the collision slow and burst damage carve big chunks out of squishy targets. Your passive grants brief invulnerability when you take lethal damage, so you can even afford some bold bait plays.
strategy.lateGame: You are the master who conducts the teamfight. Your Ultimate creates a massive, inescapable Go board. In late-game standoffs at the Tyrant or Overlord, landing that board on top of the enemy team all but guarantees the teamfight. Focus on trapping as many priority targets inside the board as possible.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, collide your black stones (Skill 1) and white stones (Skill 2) on top of the enemy backline for continuous AoE damage and slows. When enemies dive deep or clump together, deploy your Ultimate — the boundary walls trap them while your team rains damage down one-sidedly.

combos.title: Checkmate Arena
combos.description: Skill 3 -> Skill 1 -> Skill 2 -> Empowered Basic Attack. Deploy your massive Ultimate board to trap the enemy, then keep placing black and white stones inside it to trigger explosions while weaving in empowered basic attacks.

combos.title: Standard Collision Poke
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Skill 2 -> Basic Attack. Place a black stone, immediately drop a white stone nearby to trigger the magnetic collision, then follow up right away with an empowered basic attack.

strategy.commonMistakes: Whiffing your Ultimate entirely, or trapping only the enemy frontline tank inside it. Failing to keep generating collisions between black and white stones — your primary damage source.

strengths: Skill 3's one-of-a-kind power to completely wall off and isolate enemies over a huge area, together with Skill 1's vision utility, are his greatest strengths. His magic attack and empowered basic attacks also grow automatically as he collects stones over the course of the game, and his passive's invulnerability acts as a built-in safety net — his influence in late-game teamfights is enormous.
weaknesses: His main damage relies on skill combos and mark stacks, so he struggles to produce instant burst. Skill 3's board also forms with a delay, letting enemies with blink skills slip out, and with no innate escape skill of his own he is extremely weak once assassins mark him as their target.

synergy.reason: Provides movement speed buffs to compensate for Mengqi's lack of mobility, allowing quick backline dives.
Provides shields and massive CC, creating a space for Mengqi to run wild on the frontline in teamfights.

counters.reason: Silence and heavy burst damage can quickly melt Mengqi before he even has a chance to cast skills.
Team-wide CC cleanse completely nullifies Mengqi's engage and disruption potential.

passive.description:
Menki gains Mass when he uses skills. For every 10 Mass, he gains 6 physical attack, 8 physical defense and 8 magical defense.
He loses 5 Mass per second while in combat, and 15 Mass per second when out of combat.

skill1.description:
Menki uses Dream Power to gain a shield that negates 431 (175 + 150% physical attack) damage for 4s, while also dealing 371 (260 + 65% physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and increasing his Mass by 30.
This skill's cooldown is reduced by 0.5s every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack.

skill2.description:
Menki throws a Dream Bubble in the target direction and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s. After reaching its max range, the Dream Bubble returns to him.
Upon catching the Dream Bubble, he throws it again at a nearby enemy, and it returns to him after it reaches its max range.
The Dream Bubble deals 130 (130 + 25% physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and places 1 stacks of slow on them for 2s, for up to 4 stacks. The slow effect is dependent on Menki's physical attack.
After retrieving the Dream Bubble a second time, he gains 30 Mass and the bubble turns into a Dream Bomb. He can throw the Dream Bomb in a target direction to deal 100 (100 + 24% physical attack) - 550 (550 + 132% physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range of its explosion.
The longer the Dream Bubble flies, the higher the damage of the Dream Bomb, with maximum damage dealt at 5.5s of flight time.

skill3.description: Menki performs a dream roam, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path while continuously gaining Mass. He briefly gains crowd control immunity at the start of the dream roam. Using the skill again stops the roam immediately, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and launching them for 0.75s.

strategy.earlyGame: Menki is a versatile fighter/tank played in the Clash Lane or jungle. Managing Mass (his energy) is everything: higher Mass means more attack and defense, but lower movement speed. Use Skill 1's shield to shrug off enemy poke while landing heavy basic attacks to seize control of the lane.
strategy.midGame: He excels at side lane pressure and skirmishes. Throw Skill 2's bubbles to reduce enemy movement speed and attack power, making you overwhelmingly strong in 1v1 duels. Use your Ultimate's long-range dash and landing knock-up to join teamfights quickly.
strategy.lateGame: Your role shifts with your build — physical, magic, or tank. A damage build makes you a backline-shredding threat; a tank build makes you a disruptor who wreaks havoc inside the enemy formation. Either way, use your Ultimate's crowd control immunity and mobility to vault over the enemy frontline and dive priority targets directly.
strategy.teamfight: Start by throwing Skill 2 for poke and debuffs. Charge your Ultimate to cross the battlefield and dive the enemy marksman or mage with the knock-up. Immediately gain a shield and Mass with Skill 1, then batter them down with basic attacks.

combos.title: Dream Dive
combos.description: Skill 3 (charge and release) -> Skill 1 -> Basic Attack -> Skill 2. Ultimate onto the backline for the knock-up. Instantly gain a shield and Mass with Skill 1, hammer in basic attacks, and slow them with Skill 2 if they try to escape.

combos.title: Trading Shield
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Basic Attack -> Skill 2. Raise your shield to absorb the enemy's damage skills, land a heavy basic attack, then toss a bubble on your way out for the debuff.

strategy.commonMistakes: Entering fights at zero Mass, leaving yourself with neither durability nor damage. Using your Ultimate without predicting enemy movement and landing on empty ground.

synergy.reason: Da Qiao's recall and teleport skills drastically improve Gongsun Li's survivability and map presence.
Movement speed buffs and heals further enhance Gongsun Li's hit-and-run playstyle.

counters.reason: Targeted hard CC will completely shut down her mobility.
Guaranteed stuns and massive burst damage can instantly one-shot the squishy Gongsun Li.

passive.description: Arli's Basic Attacks place 1 stack of Maple on enemies for 5s, for up to 4 stacks. At max stacks, she detonates the Maples, dealing 220 (220 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage to the target and enemies near them, and placing 1 stack of Maple on them. If she uses an active skill, she can use it again within 4s to teleport to the parasol's location and retrieve it. Otherwise, she will automatically retrieve the parasol after 4s. When she isn't holding her parasol, she gains 30-60 Movement Speed and 10-20% Attack Speed (increases with level). Every time she uses a skill or retrieves her parasol, her next Basic Attack will be enhanced, launching an extra Basic Attack that deals 53 (20 + 20% physical attack) physical damage. She can stock up to 2 enhanced Basic Attacks.

skill1.description: Arli blinks in the target direction. If she is carrying her parasol, she will leave it behind at the location she blinked from.

skill2.description: Arli attacks nearby enemies twice, each attack dealing 300 (300 + 72% extra physical attack) magical damage. Using the skill also knocks down nearby enemy projectiles. If she is holding her parasol, it will fly in a circle around the location where she used the skill.

skill3.description: Arli deals 400 (400 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in the target direction and knocks them back. If she is holding her parasol, she will throw it in the same direction. Upon reaching a certain distance, the parasol will continue to fly at a slower pace.

strategy.earlyGame: Arli is the most agile Farm Lane marksman in the game, playing more like an assassin. Her entire kit revolves around managing her umbrella: each skill leaves it in place, and recasting blinks her to its location. Dash forward with Skill 1, stack your passive with basic attacks, then instantly return to your starting spot — drill this harass pattern until it's second nature.
strategy.midGame: In the mid game, her extraordinary mobility and projectile destruction make her untouchable in skirmishes. Skill 2 spins the umbrella around her, erasing every incoming enemy projectile — basic attacks and skills alike. Use it to completely nullify enemy marksman and mage burst while weaving in and out of fights.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, positioning is everything. She is extremely squishy — one piece of hard CC (a stun, for example) means instant death. Fight from the edges of teamfights. Use your Ultimate to knock back diving assassins and frontline tanks. As long as you survive, your passive's magic damage burst every 4 hits will shred even tanks.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, never stand still. Poke from unpredictable angles with Skill 1. Answer powerful enemy Ultimates (Kongming's or Hou Yi's, for example) with a reactive Skill 2 to erase them. When the enemy frontline dives in, shove them back with your Ultimate, then blink to the umbrella behind you and kite.

combos.title: Hit-and-Run Poke
combos.description: Skill 1 -> Basic Attack (x2) -> Skill 1 (recast). Dash forward from a safe position, land two quick basic attacks to apply your passive marks, then recast to return to your starting point before the enemy can retaliate.

combos.title: Self-Peel & Kite
combos.description: Skill 3 -> Basic Attack -> Skill 3 (recast) -> Skill 2. Shove the incoming threat away with your Ultimate, land a basic attack, blink to your umbrella to reposition, then block the enemy's ranged counterattack with Skill 2.

strategy.commonMistakes: Forgetting where your umbrella is and recasting straight into the middle of the enemy team. Burning Skill 2 too aggressively and losing your defense against enemy projectiles.

strengths: Every one of her skills — 1, 2, and 3 — doubles as a blink, and with Skill 2's projectile destruction and Skill 3's knockback on top, she boasts evasion and mobility that rank among the very best of any hero. Add the burst damage from her passive's mark detonations and empowered basic attacks, and she is a marksman with an exceptionally high ceiling.
weaknesses: Her skill floor is brutally high — she only reaches her true potential when the player tracks the umbrella's position at all times and executes every skill with perfect timing. And because her defense lives entirely in her evasion, her base stats are very low: targeted, guaranteed CC (a stun, for example) will delete her in an instant with no chance to respond.

synergy.reason: The link boosts her basic attack range and damage, allowing her to melt enemies from a safe distance.
Buffing a highly mobile ADC makes it incredibly easy to snowball the early game.

counters.reason: High mobility and burst damage pose a huge threat, as he can instantly wipe out both Ming and his linked ally.
Insane burst damage can delete allies before Ming even has a chance to heal them.

passive.description:
Every 5s, the next Basic Attack deals 238 (70 + 100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) magical damage and steals Health from the hit enemy, restoring 225 (225 + 40% magical attack) Health to the linked teammate and to Ming. Ming additionally recovers 4% extra Health.
Hitting a non-hero enemy unit only restores 50% Health.

skill1.description:
Ming throws his instrument. If it hits a teammate, it links to them. If it misses, it automatically links to a teammate within range. The instrument increases the linked teammate's main attack stat by 20 (20 + 10% magical attack) (1 main attack stat = 1 physical attack or 2 magical attack) and their Attack Speed by 10%.
